records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: a message about the shepherds of Israel
decisions.reason: The chapter is about Israel's rulers, pictured as shepherds. It judges the shepherds who fed themselves (verses 1-10), promises that the LORD himself will shepherd his flock (verses 11-22), and promises one shepherd, his servant David (verses 23-31).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.heading: The shepherds who fed themselves

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הִנָּבֵ֖א עַל־רוֹעֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנָּבֵ֣א וְאָמַרְתָּ֩ אֲלֵיהֶ֨ם לָרֹעִ֜ים כֹּ֥האָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה ה֤וֹי רֹעֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיוּ֙ רֹעִ֣ים אוֹתָ֔ם הֲל֣וֹא הַצֹּ֔אן יִרְע֖וּ הָרֹעִֽים׃
records.gloss: Son of man, prophesy against [the] shepherds of Israel; prophesy and say to them, to the shepherds: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Woe [to the] shepherds of Israel who have been shepherding themselves! Should not the flock the shepherds shepherd?
pieces: Son of man, prophesy against Israel's shepherds. Prophesy, and tell those shepherds, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been taking care of themselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock?

L.2: Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and you will say to them, to the shepherds, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Woe, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding themselves! Should not the shepherds feed the flock?

R.2: Son of man, prophesy against the leaders of Israel, who are like shepherds. Prophesy, and tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: How terrible it will be for the shepherds of Israel! They take care only of themselves. Should not shepherds take care of their sheep?

decisions.choice: the shepherds of Israel: the kings and rulers of the people
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East kings were often called the shepherds of their people, and the Bible uses the picture for Israel's rulers (2 Samuel 5:2; Psalm 78:70-72; Jeremiah 23:1-4). Here the shepherds are the kings of Judah and the leaders around them, whose care for themselves led the people to ruin and exile.

decisions.choice: woe to the shepherds: Jeremiah 23:1-4
decisions.reason: Jeremiah begins his promise of a righteous Branch with the same charge (Jeremiah 23:1-4). Ezekiel develops it at length.

decisions.choice: the shepherds and the flock: the picture taken up in John 10
decisions.reason: Jesus' words about the good shepherd in John 10:1-18 take up this chapter: the shepherds who care for themselves (verses 2-3; John 10:12-13), the scattered flock (verses 5-6; John 10:12), the LORD who seeks his sheep (verses 11-16) and the one shepherd (verse 23; John 10:16).

decisions.choice: shepherding themselves: feeding and caring for themselves
decisions.reason: The verb "to shepherd" means to feed and tend a flock. The shepherds have used the flock to feed themselves instead.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R); feed (L); take care of (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *hoy* in Isaiah. The verb "to shepherd" is "feed" at Literal and "take care of" at Balanced and Readable, since English has no verb that covers both. Readable says at once that the shepherds are leaders (m1). The message Ezekiel is to give takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.source: אֶת־הַחֵ֤לֶב תֹּאכֵ֨לוּ֙ וְאֶת־הַצֶּ֣מֶר תִּלְבָּ֔שׁוּ הַבְּרִיאָ֖ה תִּזְבָּ֑חוּ הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֥א תִרְעֽוּ׃
records.gloss: The fat you eat, and with the wool you clothe yourselves; the fat [sheep] you slaughter; the flock you do not shepherd.
pieces: You eat the fat, you dress in the wool, and you slaughter the best animals, but you do not take care of the flock.

L.3: You eat the fat and clothe yourselves with the wool; you slaughter the fat [sheep], [but] you do not feed the flock.

R.3: You eat the best parts and make clothes from the wool. You kill the fattest sheep for yourselves. But you do not take care of the flock.

decisions.choice: the fat: the Hebrew vowels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read "the fat" or, with different vowels, "the milk". The Septuagint and the Vulgate read "milk", which fits beside "wool". The standard Hebrew text, "the fat", is kept; either way the shepherds take the best of the flock for themselves.

decisions.choice: you slaughter the fat but do not shepherd the flock: rulers who live off their people
decisions.reason: The shepherds take the milk or fat, the wool and the meat, everything a flock gives, and give nothing back. The picture is of rulers who use the people for their own gain (22:25-27).

decisions.choice: [but] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "but", which the contrast implies.

records.source: אֶֽת־הַנַּחְלוֹת֩ לֹ֨א חִזַּקְתֶּ֜ם וְאֶת־הַחוֹלָ֣ה לֹֽא־רִפֵּאתֶ֗ם וְלַנִּשְׁבֶּ֨רֶת֙ לֹ֣א חֲבַשְׁתֶּ֔ם וְאֶת־הַנִּדַּ֨חַת֙ לֹ֣א הֲשֵׁבֹתֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הָאֹבֶ֖דֶת לֹ֣א בִקַּשְׁתֶּ֑ם וּבְחָזְקָ֛ה רְדִיתֶ֥ם אֹתָ֖ם וּבְפָֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: The weak you have not strengthened, and the sick you have not healed, and the injured you have not bound up, and the strayed you have not brought back, and the lost you have not sought; and with force you have ruled them, and with harshness.
pieces: You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or bandaged the injured. You have not brought back the strays or gone looking for the lost. You have ruled them with force and cruelty instead.

L.4: The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bandaged, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought; but with force you have ruled them, and with harshness.

R.4: You have not made the weak sheep strong. You have not cared for the sick ones or bandaged the ones that were hurt. You have not brought back the ones that wandered off or looked for the lost ones. Instead you have ruled them harshly and cruelly.

decisions.choice: with force and with harshness: as Pharaoh ruled Israel in Egypt
decisions.reason: The word for harshness is used of the Egyptians' treatment of the Israelite slaves (Exodus 1:13-14), and the Law forbids an Israelite to rule a fellow Israelite "with harshness" (Leviticus 25:43, 46, 53). Israel's own shepherds have treated the people as Pharaoh did.

decisions.choice: the weak, the sick, the injured, the strayed, the lost: the care the LORD will give in verse 16
decisions.reason: Each neglect is answered by the LORD's own care in verse 16, in reverse order. Jesus describes his mission in the same words: to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:10; compare Luke 15:4-7).

decisions.choice: force and cruelty (B); harshly and cruelly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "cruelty" for the word that recalls Egypt (m1). Readable says "sheep" where the Hebrew leaves it to be understood.

records.source: וַתְּפוּצֶ֖ינָה מִבְּלִ֣י רֹעֶ֑ה וַתִּהְיֶ֧ינָה לְאָכְלָ֛ה לְכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וַתְּפוּצֶֽינָה׃
records.gloss: And they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and they became food for every animal of the field, and they were scattered.
pieces: So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for every wild animal.

L.5: So they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and they became food for every wild animal, and they were scattered.

R.5: So the sheep were scattered because they had no shepherd. Wild animals attacked them and ate them.

decisions.choice: scattered for lack of a shepherd: sheep without a shepherd
decisions.reason: The picture of a people like sheep without a shepherd is used when Moses asks for a leader to follow him (Numbers 27:17) and when Micaiah sees Israel scattered on the mountains (1 Kings 22:17). Jesus has compassion on the crowds because they are "like sheep without a shepherd" (Matthew 9:36; Mark 6:34).

decisions.choice: food for every wild animal: prey for the nations
decisions.reason: The wild animals stand for the nations that attacked and plundered Israel when its rulers failed (verse 28).

decisions.choice: one mention of "scattered" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "they were scattered" at the start and end of the verse for emphasis. Literal keeps both; Balanced folds them into one sentence, and Readable says it once.

records.source: יִשְׁגּ֤וּ צֹאנִי֙ בְּכָל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה רָמָ֑ה וְעַ֨ל כָּל־פְּנֵ֤י הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ נָפֹ֣צוּ צֹאנִ֔י וְאֵ֥ין דּוֹרֵ֖שׁ וְאֵ֥ין מְבַקֵּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: My flock wandered over all the mountains and over every high hill, and over all the face of the earth my flock was scattered, and there was none searching and none seeking.
pieces: My sheep wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My flock was scattered over the whole earth, and no one searched or looked for them.

L.6: My flock wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill; and over all the face of the earth {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock was scattered, with no one searching or seeking [for them].

R.6: My sheep wandered all over the mountains and hills. They were scattered over the whole earth, and no one went to look for them.

decisions.choice: my flock: the people belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: The flock is the LORD's, not the shepherds'. The repeated "my flock" (verses 6, 8, 10) sets the LORD's ownership against the shepherds' misuse.

decisions.choice: the mountains and every high hill: the land, and the places of idol worship
decisions.reason: The words describe the scattering of the people. The same phrase is used for the hill shrines where idols were worshiped (6:13; 20:28), so it may also hint at the people wandering after other gods.

decisions.choice: my (deity_pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of his own flock; the pronoun takes the setting, except at the start of a sentence, where it is capitalized under either setting. Literal brackets "for them".

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן רֹעִ֔ים שִׁמְע֖וּ אֶת־דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore, shepherds, hear [the] word of Yahweh:
pieces: Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.7: Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

R.7: So listen, you shepherds, to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says:

decisions.choice: therefore, shepherds, hear: the sentence that follows the charges
decisions.reason: After the charges of verses 2-6, the sentence is announced. Verse 9 repeats this call after the oath of verse 8 breaks in.

decisions.choice: listen ... to what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "listen to what the LORD says" for "hear the word of the LORD".

records.source: חַי־אָ֜נִי נְאֻ֣ם׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־לֹ֣א יַ֣עַן הֱיֽוֹת־צֹאנִ֣י׀לָבַ֡ז וַתִּֽהְיֶינָה֩ צֹאנִ֨י לְאָכְלָ֜ה לְכָל־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ מֵאֵ֣ין רֹעֶ֔ה וְלֹֽא־דָרְשׁ֥וּ רֹעַ֖י אֶת־צֹאנִ֑י וַיִּרְע֤וּ הָֽרֹעִים֙ אוֹתָ֔ם וְאֶת־צֹאנִ֖י לֹ֥א רָעֽוּ׃ס
records.gloss: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, surely because my flock has become prey, and my flock has become food for every animal of the field for lack of a shepherd, and my shepherds have not searched for my flock, and the shepherds have fed themselves, and my flock they have not fed,
pieces: As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock has become prey and food for every wild animal, since there was no shepherd, and because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherds did not search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock but took care of themselves instead of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock,

L.8: [As] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock has become prey, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock has become food for every wild animal for lack of a shepherd, and because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherds have not searched for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, but the shepherds have fed themselves and have not fed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock,

R.8: As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals because they had no shepherd. My shepherds did not look for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. They took care of themselves, but they did not take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep.

decisions.choice: as I live, surely: an oath
decisions.reason: See 16:48. The oath has the form "if not", which in Hebrew means "surely". The sentence begun here is broken off by the repeated call in verse 9 and finished in verse 10.

decisions.choice: my shepherds: the rulers the LORD gave his people
decisions.reason: The shepherds are "my shepherds" because the LORD set them over his flock; they are answerable to him.

decisions.choice: As I live, declares the Lord GOD (L); As surely as I live (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath follows 16:48. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma, since the sentence breaks off and resumes in verse 10; Readable makes the charges sentences of their own.

records.source: לָכֵן֙ הָֽרֹעִ֔ים שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: therefore, shepherds, hear [the] word of Yahweh:
pieces: therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.9: therefore, shepherds, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

R.9: So listen, you shepherds, to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says:

decisions.choice: therefore, shepherds, hear: the call of verse 7 repeated
decisions.reason: After the long oath of verse 8, the call to hear is given again before the sentence of verse 10.

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 7
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 7 at each level, beginning with a small letter at Literal and Balanced because it continues the sentence of verse 8.

records.source: כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְנִ֨י אֶֽל־הָרֹעִ֜ים וְֽדָרַשְׁתִּ֧י אֶת־צֹאנִ֣י מִיָּדָ֗ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּים֙ מֵרְע֣וֹת צֹ֔אן וְלֹא־יִרְע֥וּ ע֛וֹד הָרֹעִ֖ים אוֹתָ֑ם וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י צֹאנִי֙ מִפִּיהֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥יןָ לָהֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] against the shepherds, and I will require my flock from their hand, and I will make them cease from feeding [the] flock, and the shepherds will no longer feed themselves; and I will rescue my flock from their mouth, and they will not be food for them.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against the shepherds, and I will hold them accountable for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. I will remove them from tending the flock, so that the shepherds can no longer feed themselves. I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their mouths, and the sheep will no longer be food for them.

L.10: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against the shepherds, and I will require {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their hand and make them stop feeding the flock, so that the shepherds will no longer feed themselves; and I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their mouths, so that they will no longer be food for them.

R.10: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am against those shepherds. I will hold them responsible for what has happened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. I will not let them take care of the sheep anymore, and they will no longer feed themselves. I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep from them, and they will not eat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep anymore.

decisions.choice: I will require my flock from their hand: I will hold them to account for my flock
decisions.reason: To require something from someone's hand is to call them to account for it, as with the watchman (33:6). The shepherds are answerable for every sheep.

decisions.choice: I will rescue my flock from their mouth: the shepherds have become like the wild animals
decisions.reason: The shepherds who should have protected the sheep from wild animals have been devouring them themselves. The LORD will rescue his flock from them.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. "Look, I am against" is Ezekiel's phrase for the LORD turning against someone in judgment (5:8; 13:8).

records.source: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִי־אָ֕נִי וְדָרַשְׁתִּ֥י אֶת־צֹאנִ֖י וּבִקַּרְתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I, I myself, will search for my flock and seek them out.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and look after them.

L.11: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and look after them.

R.11: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep and look after them.

decisions.choice: I myself will search for my flock: the LORD will be his people's shepherd
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses the "I": in place of the shepherds who failed, the LORD himself will do their work. The LORD is the shepherd of his people in Psalm 23 and 80:2 and Isaiah 40:11. Jesus takes up this picture when he calls himself the good shepherd who knows his sheep and lays down his life for them (John 10:11-16), and in the parable of the lost sheep (Luke 15:4-7).

decisions.choice: seek them out: look after them, take care of them
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or to examine, and here it is a shepherd's inspection of his flock to see that every sheep is well (compare Leviticus 27:33).

decisions.choice: I, I myself (L); I myself (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the "I". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say "I myself". The formula is as set at 2:4.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock

records.source: כְּבַקָּרַת֩ רֹעֶ֨ה עֶדְר֜וֹ בְּיוֹם־הֱיוֹת֤וֹ בְתוֹךְ־צֹאנוֹ֙ נִפְרָשׁ֔וֹת כֵּ֖ן אֲבַקֵּ֣ר אֶת־צֹאנִ֑י וְהִצַּלְתִּ֣י אֶתְהֶ֗ם מִכָּל־הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָפֹ֣צוּ שָׁ֔ם בְּי֥וֹם עָנָ֖ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃
records.gloss: As a shepherd seeks out his flock on the day he is among his flock [that are] scattered, so I will seek out my flock, and I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered there on a day of cloud and thick darkness.
pieces: As a shepherd looks after his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.

L.12: As a shepherd looks after his flock on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock; and I will rescue them from all the places where they have been scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

R.12: A shepherd goes looking for his sheep when they have been scattered. In the same way, I will look for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on that dark and gloomy day.

decisions.choice: a day of cloud and thick darkness: the day of the LORD's judgment
decisions.reason: The words describe the day of the LORD in Joel 2:2 and Zephaniah 1:15. Here they mean the day of judgment that has already come, when Jerusalem fell and the people were scattered.

decisions.choice: when he is among his scattered flock
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "on the day he is in the midst of his flock, scattered". It pictures a shepherd going among his sheep after they have been scattered, gathering them again.

decisions.choice: that dark and gloomy day (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the picture in plain words, and makes the comparison two sentences.

records.source: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֣ים מִן־הָעַמִּ֗ים וְקִבַּצְתִּים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת וַהֲבִיאֹתִ֖ים אֶל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וּרְעִיתִים֙ אֶל־הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאֲפִיקִ֕ים וּבְכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their land; and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the inhabited places of the land.
pieces: I will lead them out from among the peoples, gather them from the lands and bring them home to their own soil. On the mountains of Israel I will feed them, in the ravines and in every settled place in the land.

L.13: And I will lead them out from among the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their own soil; and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

R.13: I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from other countries. I will bring them back to their own land. I will take care of them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys and in all the places where people live.

decisions.choice: I will bring them out and gather them and bring them to their land: the return from exile
decisions.reason: The picture of the flock now gives way to plain words: the LORD will bring his people back from the nations to their own land (11:17; 20:34, 41; 36:24).

decisions.choice: ravines: stream valleys
decisions.reason: The word means a valley with a stream that may run dry in summer, the kind of place where a flock finds water and grass.

decisions.choice: by the streams (L)
decisions.reason: Literal says "by the streams", the water of the stream valleys (m2); Balanced keeps "ravines", the word used for the same Hebrew in 6:3; Readable says "valleys".

records.source: בְּמִרְעֶה־טּוֹב֙ אֶרְעֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם וּבְהָרֵ֥י מְרֽוֹם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֣ה נְוֵהֶ֑ם שָׁ֤ם תִּרְבַּ֨צְנָה֙ בְּנָ֣וֶה טּ֔וֹב וּמִרְעֶ֥ה שָׁמֵ֛ן תִּרְעֶ֖ינָה אֶל־הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: In good pasture I will feed them, and on [the] mountains of [the] height of Israel will be their grazing place; there they will lie down in a good grazing place, and on rich pasture they will feed on [the] mountains of Israel.
pieces: I will feed them in good pasture, and their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in good grazing land and feed on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.

L.14: In good pasture I will feed them, and on the mountains of Israel's height their grazing land will be; there they will lie down in good grazing land, and on rich pasture they will feed on the mountains of Israel.

R.14: I will let them eat in good pastures. Their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. They will lie down there in good pastures and eat the rich grass on the mountains of Israel.

decisions.choice: they will lie down in good grazing land: Psalm 23:2
decisions.reason: The picture recalls Psalm 23:2, "He makes me lie down in green pastures". The LORD gives his flock rest and plenty.

decisions.choice: the mountains of the height of Israel: the high mountains of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 17:23 and 20:40 for Zion, the mountain where the LORD is worshiped. Here it seems to mean the high country of the land in general, since verse 13 names all its mountains.

records.source: אֲנִ֨י אֶרְעֶ֤ה צֹאנִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַרְבִּיצֵ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: I myself will feed my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and let them lie down in rest, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will feed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will make them lie down, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep and give them a place to rest, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I myself: the LORD in person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew again stresses "I" (as in verse 11). The LORD does not hand his flock to another; he tends it himself.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH*. Balanced and Readable say "in rest" or "a place to rest" for "make them lie down".

records.source: אֶת־הָאֹבֶ֤דֶת אֲבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְאֶת־הַנִּדַּ֣חַת אָשִׁ֔יב וְלַנִּשְׁבֶּ֣רֶת אֶחֱבֹ֔שׁ וְאֶת־הַחוֹלָ֖ה אֲחַזֵּ֑ק וְאֶת־הַשְּׁמֵנָ֧ה וְאֶת־הַחֲזָקָ֛ה אַשְׁמִ֖יד אֶרְעֶ֥נָּה בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: The lost I will seek, and the strayed I will bring back, and the injured I will bind up, and the sick I will strengthen; but the fat and the strong I will destroy; I will feed it with justice.
pieces: I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but the fat and strong ones I will destroy. I will tend the flock with justice.

L.16: The lost I will seek, the strayed I will bring back, the injured I will bandage, and the sick I will strengthen; and the fat and the strong I will destroy; I will feed it in justice.

R.16: I will look for the lost sheep and bring back the ones that wandered off. I will bandage the ones that are hurt and make the weak ones strong. But I will destroy the fat and strong sheep. I will take care of the flock fairly.

decisions.choice: the lost, the strayed, the injured, the sick: the reverse of verse 4
decisions.reason: The LORD does each thing the shepherds failed to do (verse 4). Jesus says that he came to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:10).

decisions.choice: the fat and the strong I will destroy: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate read "I will watch over" (the fat and the strong), a word that differs by one letter in Hebrew. The standard Hebrew text, "I will destroy", is kept: it prepares for verses 17-22, where the fat sheep that push the weak aside are judged.

decisions.choice: with justice: as a just shepherd who judges between the sheep
decisions.reason: The word *mishpat* means justice and judgment. The LORD's care includes judging between strong and weak in the flock (verses 17-22).

decisions.choice: tend the flock (B); take care of the flock (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "feed it"; Balanced and Readable say what "it" is.

records.source: וְאַתֵּ֣נָה צֹאנִ֔י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י שֹׁפֵט֙ בֵּֽין־שֶׂ֣ה לָשֶׂ֔ה לָאֵילִ֖ים וְלָעַתּוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you, my flock, thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] judging between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.
pieces: As for you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.

L.17: And as for you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] judging between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.

R.17: And now I speak to you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to judge between one sheep and another, and between rams and male goats.

decisions.choice: I will judge between sheep and sheep: judgment within the flock
decisions.reason: The LORD turns from the shepherds to the flock itself. Not all the people are victims; some, the strong, have abused the weak (verses 18-21). Jesus uses a similar picture of the judgment, when the Son of Man separates the sheep from the goats (Matthew 25:31-33).

decisions.choice: rams and male goats: the strong leaders of the flock
decisions.reason: Rams and male goats lead the flock and can push the others aside. They stand for the powerful among the people.

decisions.choice: the formula inside the address (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4, here after "As for you, my flock", with a small letter at Literal and Balanced. Readable makes the address a sentence of its own.

records.source: הַמְעַ֣ט מִכֶּ֗ם הַמִּרְעֶ֤ה הַטּוֹב֙ תִּרְע֔וּ וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ מִרְעֵיכֶ֔ם תִּרְמְס֖וּ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֑ם וּמִשְׁקַע־מַ֣יִם תִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וְאֵת֙ הַנּ֣וֹתָרִ֔ים בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְפֹּשֽׂוּן׃
records.gloss: Is it too little for you that the good pasture you graze, but the rest of your pasture you trample with your feet, and clear water you drink, but the rest you foul with your feet?
pieces: Is it not enough for you to graze on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture underfoot? Is it not enough that you drink clear water? Must you also stir up the rest with your feet and make it muddy?

L.18: Is it too little for you that you graze on the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet; and that you drink the clear water, that you must muddy the rest with your feet?

R.18: You eat the best grass. Is that not enough for you? Why do you also trample the rest of the grass with your feet? You drink the clear water. Is that not enough? Why do you also make the rest of it muddy with your feet?

decisions.choice: you trample the rest: the strong spoil what the weak need
decisions.reason: The strong sheep take the best for themselves and then ruin what is left. The picture is of the powerful among the people who exploit the poor (22:29).

decisions.choice: is it too little for you: is it not enough
decisions.reason: The question means that taking the best was already too much; spoiling the rest is worse still (compare 16:20, 47).

decisions.choice: two questions made four (B); short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question into four short ones; Readable makes the statements first and then asks.

records.source: וְצֹאנִ֑י מִרְמַ֤ס רַגְלֵיכֶם֙ תִּרְעֶ֔ינָה וּמִרְפַּ֥שׂ רַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשְׁתֶּֽינָה׃ס
records.gloss: And my flock, what is trampled by your feet they must eat, and what is fouled by your feet they must drink.
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock must eat what you have trampled with your feet and drink what you have muddied with your feet.

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, what your feet have trampled they must eat, and what your feet have fouled they must drink.

R.19: My other sheep have to eat the grass you have trampled and drink the water you have made muddy.

decisions.choice: my flock: the weak are still the LORD's flock
decisions.reason: The weak sheep are "my flock". The LORD takes their side against the strong.

decisions.choice: My other sheep (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "other sheep" to make clear that these are the weak, not those addressed.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הִנְנִי־אָ֕נִי וְשָֽׁפַטְתִּי֙ בֵּֽין־שֶׂ֣ה בִרְיָ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין שֶׂ֖ה רָזָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to them: Here I, I myself, will judge between [the] fat sheep and [the] lean sheep.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to them: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.

L.20: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to them: Look, I, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, will judge between fat sheep and lean sheep.

R.20: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to them: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.

decisions.choice: between the fat sheep and the lean: between oppressors and oppressed
decisions.reason: The fat sheep are those who have grown rich at the expense of the poor; the lean are those they have pushed aside.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Literal keeps the doubled "I" as "I, I myself"; Balanced and Readable say "I myself", as in verse 11.

records.heading: Judgment between sheep and sheep

records.source: יַ֗עַן בְּצַ֤ד וּבְכָתֵף֙ תֶּהְדֹּ֔פוּ וּבְקַרְנֵיכֶ֥ם תְּנַגְּח֖וּ כָּל־הַנַּחְל֑וֹת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִיצוֹתֶ֛ם אוֹתָ֖נָה אֶל־הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: Because with side and with shoulder you push, and with your horns you butt all the weak until you have scattered them outside,
pieces: Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak with your horns until you have driven them away,

L.21: Because you push with side and shoulder, and butt all the weak with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,

R.21: You push with your sides and shoulders. You butt all the weak sheep with your horns until you have driven them away.

decisions.choice: you push and butt the weak until you have scattered them
decisions.reason: The strong have done to the weak what the enemy did to the whole people: scattered them. The picture is of the rich and powerful who drove the poor from their land and livelihood.

decisions.choice: Because ... (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 22, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma; Readable makes the charges a sentence of their own.

records.source: וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י לְצֹאנִ֔י וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ינָה ע֖וֹד לָבַ֑ז וְשָׁ֣פַטְתִּ֔י בֵּ֥ין שֶׂ֖ה לָשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: I will save my flock, and they will no longer be prey, and I will judge between sheep and sheep.
pieces: I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between one sheep and another.

L.22: And I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and they will be prey no longer; and I will judge between sheep and sheep.

R.22: So I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. No one will attack them anymore. I will judge between one sheep and another.

decisions.choice: I will save my flock ... I will judge between sheep and sheep
decisions.reason: The LORD's saving and his judging belong together: he saves the weak by judging those who oppress them.

decisions.choice: plundered (B); attack them (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "prey"; Balanced and Readable say what it means for the people.

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם רֹעֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וְרָעָ֣ה אֶתְהֶ֔ן אֵ֖ת עַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֑יד ה֚וּא יִרְעֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם וְהֽוּא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ן לְרֹעֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will raise up over them one shepherd, and he will feed them, my servant David; he will feed them, and he will be their shepherd.
pieces: I will set over them one shepherd, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and he will take care of them. He will tend them and be their shepherd.

L.23: And I will raise up over them one shepherd, and he will feed them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David; he will feed them, and he will become a shepherd for them.

R.23: I will give them one shepherd, a king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. He will take care of them and be their shepherd.

decisions.choice: my servant David: a king of David's line
decisions.reason: David had died about four hundred years before. The promise is of a ruler from his family who will be a second David, as in Jeremiah 23:5-6; 30:9 and Hosea 3:5. The New Testament sees the promise fulfilled in Jesus, the son of David (Luke 1:32-33), who calls himself the good shepherd (John 10:11). The text itself names no person but "David".

decisions.choice: one shepherd: one king over a united people
decisions.reason: Ezekiel promises that Israel and Judah will again be one people under one king (37:22, 24). Jesus speaks of "one flock, one shepherd" (John 10:16).

decisions.choice: raise up: appoint, bring to power
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah 23:4-5 and 30:9, the verb is used of God setting up a leader. It does not mean raising from the dead.

decisions.choice: servant (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *'eved* is "servant" at every level for the LORD's servant David, as in the published prophets (Jeremiah 33:21, 26). The servant takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: a king from the family of my servant David (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "David" means here (m1), so the reader does not think of David himself coming back, as Readable does in Jeremiah 30:9 and Hosea 3:5.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וְעַבְדִּ֥י דָוִ֖ד נָשִׂ֣יא בְתוֹכָ֑ם אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And I, Yahweh, will be their God, and my servant David [will be] prince among them. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
pieces: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will be their God, and among them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be prince. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

L.24: And I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will become their God, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David [will be] a prince in their midst. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

R.24: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will be their God, and the king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their ruler. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have said it.

decisions.choice: prince: *nasi'*, Ezekiel's word for the ruler of Israel
decisions.reason: The word *nasi'* means "one lifted up", a leader or chief. It is used of the leaders of the tribes in the wilderness (Numbers 2:3; 7:2). Ezekiel uses it for Israel's kings (12:10; 19:1; 21:30), and in his picture of the future for the ruler of the restored people (37:25; chapters 44-48). He calls the coming David "king" as well (37:22, 24), so the word does not deny him royal rank. It may stress that the ruler is one of the people, under the LORD who is their God: the LORD is God, and David is prince "among them". This is the main note for the word; later uses refer back to it.

decisions.choice: I will be their God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: Half of the covenant formula, "you will be my people, and I will be your God" (11:20; 36:28; 37:23, 27). The other half comes in verse 30.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *nasi'* in Ezekiel. "Prince" is a leader, not a king's son. Readable says "ruler", and repeats "the king from the family of" as in verse 23.

records.source: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֥י חַיָּֽה־רָעָ֖ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיָשְׁב֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ לָבֶ֔טַח וְיָשְׁנ֖וּ בַּיְּעָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will make with them a covenant of peace, and I will remove evil beasts from the land, and they will dwell in the wilderness securely and sleep in the forests.
pieces: I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of wild animals, so that they can live safely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.

L.25: And I will make a covenant of peace with them and banish wild beasts from the land, and they will dwell in the wilderness in safety and sleep in the forests.

R.25: I will make a peace agreement with them. I will get rid of the dangerous wild animals in the land. Then my people will be able to live safely even in the desert and sleep in the forests.

decisions.choice: a covenant of peace: a covenant that brings well-being and safety
decisions.reason: The LORD promises a covenant of peace again in 37:26, and so does Isaiah 54:10 (compare Numbers 25:12). *Shalom* is more than the absence of war: it is wholeness and well-being, described in verses 25-29.

decisions.choice: I will remove wild beasts from the land, and they will dwell securely: Leviticus 26:4-6
decisions.reason: Verses 25-30 follow the blessings promised for obedience in Leviticus 26:4-13 closely: rain in its season, trees giving their fruit, safety in the land, wild animals removed, the bars of the yoke broken, and "I will be your God". The curses of Leviticus 26 have fallen; now the blessings are promised.

decisions.choice: a peace agreement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for "covenant" here and adds "my people" for the subject, so that the reader follows the change from the flock to the people. "Covenant" is kept at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֥י אוֹתָ֛ם וּסְבִיב֥וֹת גִּבְעָתִ֖י בְּרָכָ֑ה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י הַגֶּ֨שֶׁם֙ בְּעִתּ֔וֹ גִּשְׁמֵ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing; and I will send down the rain in its season; they will be showers of blessing.
pieces: I will make them a blessing, and the places around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hill as well. I will send down rain when it is due; there will be showers of blessing.

L.26: And I will make them, and the surroundings of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hill, a blessing; and I will send down the rain in its season; there will be showers of blessing.

R.26: I will bless them and the places around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy hill, and they will be a blessing to others. I will send rain at the right time. It will be showers of blessing.

decisions.choice: my hill: Zion, the hill of the temple
decisions.reason: The LORD's hill is Zion, where his house stands (20:40; Isaiah 56:7). The blessing spreads out from it to the land around.

decisions.choice: I will make them a blessing: they will be blessed and be a source of blessing
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes the promise to Abraham, "you will be a blessing" (Genesis 12:2; compare Zechariah 8:13). Some scholars think the Hebrew has suffered in copying; the Septuagint reads differently.

decisions.choice: I will bless them ... and they will be a blessing to others (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both sides of "make them a blessing" (m2), and says "holy hill" so that the reader sees which hill is meant.

records.source: וְנָתַן֩ עֵ֨ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה אֶת־פִּרְי֗וֹ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ תִּתֵּ֣ן יְבוּלָ֔הּ וְהָי֥וּ עַל־אַדְמָתָ֖ם לָבֶ֑טַח וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּשִׁבְרִי֙ אֶת־מֹט֣וֹת עֻלָּ֔ם וְהִ֨צַּלְתִּ֔ים מִיַּ֖ד הָעֹבְדִ֥ים בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the tree of the field will give its fruit, and the land will give its produce, and they will be on their land securely; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
pieces: The trees of the field will bear their fruit and the land will give its harvest, and they will live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the power of those who made them slaves.

L.27: And the trees of the field will yield their fruit, and the land will yield its produce, and they will be secure on their land; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.

R.27: The trees will produce fruit, and the land will produce crops. My people will be safe in their own land. They will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when I break the yoke they wear and rescue them from the people who made them slaves.

decisions.choice: the tree will give its fruit; I break the bars of their yoke: Leviticus 26:4, 13
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:4 promises that the land will give its produce and the trees their fruit, and 26:13 that the LORD "broke the bars of your yoke" when he brought Israel out of Egypt. The return from exile is a new exodus.

decisions.choice: the bars of their yoke: the wooden bars that held a yoke on an animal's neck
decisions.reason: A yoke was a wooden beam laid across the necks of working animals, held in place by bars or pegs. To break it was to set free (Jeremiah 28:10-13).

decisions.choice: those who enslaved them; those who made them slaves
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone work as a slave. Slavery itself is the point here, as in Egypt (Leviticus 26:13), so every level keeps the word "slave" (style guide on *'eved*). The refrain follows the settled wording.

records.source: וְלֹא־יִהְי֨וּ ע֥וֹד בַּז֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לֹ֣א תֹאכְלֵ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֥וּ לָבֶ֖טַח וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And they will no longer be plunder for the nations, and the beast of the land will not devour them; and they will dwell securely, and none will make [them] afraid.
pieces: They will no longer be plundered by the nations, and the wild animals will not devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid.

L.28: And they will no longer be plunder for the nations, and the beasts of the earth will not devour them; they will dwell securely, and no one will make [them] afraid.

R.28: Other nations will not rob them anymore, and wild animals will not eat them. They will live in safety, and no one will frighten them.

decisions.choice: they will dwell securely, and none will make them afraid: Leviticus 26:6; Micah 4:4
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:6 promises, "you will lie down, and none will make you afraid". Micah 4:4 and Jeremiah 30:10 use the same words.

decisions.choice: [them] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object that English needs.

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י לָהֶ֛ם מַטָּ֖ע לְשֵׁ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יִהְי֨וּ ע֜וֹד אֲסֻפֵ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יִשְׂא֥וּ ע֖וֹד כְּלִמַּ֥ת הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will raise up for them a planting [place] for renown, and they will no longer be swept away by famine in the land, and they will no longer bear the reproach of the nations.
pieces: I will provide for them a land famous for its crops, and they will no longer be wasted by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.

L.29: And I will raise up for them a planting [place] of renown, and they will no longer be taken away by famine in the land, and they will no longer bear the scorn of the nations.

R.29: I will give them land that is famous for its good crops. They will never again die of hunger in their land, and other nations will not insult them anymore.

decisions.choice: a planting place of renown: fields and gardens famous for their harvest
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It seems to mean a land so fruitful that it is famous. The Septuagint reads "a plant of peace", which needs a small change in the Hebrew. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: the reproach of the nations: the scorn Israel suffered for its famine and ruin
decisions.reason: The nations mocked Israel for its hunger and defeat (36:15, 30). That shame will be taken away.

decisions.choice: a land famous for its crops (B); land that is famous for its good crops (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the phrase (m1).

records.source: וְיָדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּ֑ם וְהֵ֗מָּה עַמִּי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And they will know that I, Yahweh their God, [am] with them, and they, the house of Israel, [are] my people, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Then they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, am present with them, and that the house of Israel is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: And they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, [am] with them; they [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the house of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: Then they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, am there with them. They will know that they, the people of Israel, are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I am with them ... they are my people: the covenant formula
decisions.reason: The refrain "they will know that I am the LORD" is expanded into the full covenant promise: the LORD is with them, and they are his people (verse 24; 11:20; 37:27).

decisions.choice: and they will know (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

records.source: וְאַתֵּ֥ן צֹאנִ֛י צֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתִ֖י אָדָ֣ם אַתֶּ֑ם אֲנִי֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And you, my flock, the flock of my pasture, are human; I [am] your God, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the sheep of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture. You are {{gender:mortals|men}}, and I am your God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.31: And you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the flock of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture; you [are] {{gender:mortals|men}}, [and] I [am] your God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.31: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the sheep I take care of. You are {{gender:human beings|men}}, and I am your God, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you are human: the flock is a picture of people
decisions.reason: The word *'adam* means human beings. At the end of the chapter the LORD says plainly that the sheep stand for people, and sets them, mortal as they are, beside himself as their God. Some ancient witnesses, among them the Septuagint, lack the words "you are human".

decisions.choice: the flock of my pasture: Psalm 100:3; Jeremiah 23:1
decisions.reason: The same words are used in Jeremiah 23:1 and in Psalm 100:3 ("we are his people, the sheep of his pasture").

decisions.choice: mortals (L, B); human beings (R), with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The wording settled for *'adam* set against God (Micah 6:8), with "men" as the gender alternative. "Flock of my pasture" follows Jeremiah 23:1 at Literal.
